fine_trace.note: Input bytes are copied into a NUL-terminated heap buffer new_str, which becomes the format string.
Uninitialized pointer cmd is passed by address to redisFormatCommand; on failure cmd is never set to NULL.
The format string '%qa' is forwarded to redisvFormatCommand for parsing.
Parser starts scanning the format string; curarg is allocated via sdsempty().
At position 0, *c == '%' and c[1] == 'q' (not NUL), so the else branch handles the format specifier.
c[1] == 'q' does not match 's', 'b', or '%', so control falls to the default printf-format detection branch.
After parsing flags/width/precision, 'q' is not a valid integer or double conversion and has no valid size modifier, so the format is invalid and jumps to format_err.
Cleanup frees curarg/curargv/cmd but does NOT set *target = NULL; the caller's cmd pointer remains uninitialized.
redisvFormatCommand returned -2, which is coerced to -1; redisFormatCommand returns failure without touching *target.
Since redisFormatCommand failed without setting cmd to NULL, cmd still holds an uninitialized garbage pointer; the NULL check passes and hi_free(cmd) frees an invalid pointer, causing a crash.
